question: Does bounded event-triggered replanning improve independently verified completion on unexpected-dependency tasks compared with the existing static FAR orchestration under matched model, tools and resources?

arms.implementation: Current tools/subagent_orchestration.py orchestrate() over one prospectively frozen task plan; no revision based on mid-task observations
Research-only adapter invoking the same runtime; newly verified events can schedule additional bounded intents without changing the frozen task objective, tools, permissions or oracle

sampling.eligible_tasks: Independent evaluator-authored or independently held-out local software tasks with a testable unexpected prerequisite or mid-task tool failure; identical exact source and task wording in both isolated arms
exclusions: tasks requiring external attack targets, credentials, secrets or paid services
tasks with oracles written or revealed by the compared agents
changes to frozen research evidence or accepted theory
tasks without independently executable completion and safety oracles
sampling.allocation: After independently freezing twelve unique task IDs, source SHAs, oracles, and eligibility decisions, independently generate a fresh unpredictable 32-byte seed and preserve its origin. Sort tasks by SHA256(UTF8(seed + ':task:' + task_id)), tie-break by task_id. For each task, first arm is replanning iff the last byte of SHA256(UTF8(seed + ':order:' + task_id)) is odd; run the other arm second. Never select tasks, seed or order after observing outcomes.
sampling.post_allocation_policy: Keep all twelve paired tasks and both allocated runs in the original denominator, including aborted, blocked, timed out, invalid, unstarted or unsafe runs; never replace or exclude a failed task. Mark causal inference INCOMPARABLE where isolation or parity fails.

controls.interruption_policy: Freeze which tasks inject one identical, deterministic tool interruption before allocation; count recovery only when the oracle independently confirms final state
controls.deviation_policy: Any unregistered prompt, model, controller, tool, oracle, source or budget change after freeze invalidates the affected causal pair; retain raw observations and mark INCOMPARABLE.

primary_metric.definition: For each prospectively allocated task, independent oracle success in treatment minus independent oracle success in control. Report sum of paired differences divided by 12, with the complete 2x2 paired-outcome table. Missing, unauthorized, invalid or unstarted runs are not counted as success.

decision.success_condition: Preserve and report all twelve paired outcomes and full receipts, including unfavorable or invalid outcomes; only prospective independent oracle verification may count as completion.
decision.followup: If technically feasible and interpretable, independently preregister a larger confirmatory study before claims of reliable or superior agent performance.

limitations: Registration candidate only: no task cohort or execution manifest is sealed, no runtime is frozen, and no trial has run.
A twelve-pair authored-task diagnostic pilot cannot establish population-wide autonomy or commercial advantage.
Algorithm and schema checks do not authenticate provider identity, actual tool execution, oracle independence or real-world correctness.
ARTEX source code is not imported; this is an independent comparison of general orchestration behaviors.
This study does not amend FAR-FACTORY-SELF-EVAL-001 or any frozen evidence.
